summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Helen Vlachos, the only child of Georgios Vlachos, founder of the Greek newspaper Kathimerini in 1919. It notes her work as a journalist at her father's paper, including coverage of the 1936 Berlin Olympics. It also records that her father closed Kathimerini rather than cooperate with the Nazi occupation government, and that she worked as a nurse during the war.
one_line: Biographical note on Helen Vlachos, journalist and nurse, daughter of Kathimerini founder Georgios Vlachos.
key_facts: Helen Vlachos was the daughter and only child of Georgios Vlachos.
Georgios Vlachos founded the newspaper Kathimerini in 1919.
Kathimerini is described in the note as one of Greece's premier newspapers.
Helen Vlachos worked as a journalist in her father's newspaper.
Helen Vlachos covered the Berlin Olympics in 1936.
During World War II, Georgios Vlachos refused to cooperate with the Nazi occupation government.
Georgios Vlachos closed down Kathimerini during World War II rather than cooperate with the Nazi occupation government.
During the war, Helen Vlachos worked as a nurse.
